actions.description: Advance the simulated world by a bounded number of fixed timesteps, optionally applying an action for each step, and return the resulting observation and terminal flags.

facts.text: The project provides a mapping and navigation package for Unitree quadruped robots in Gazebo.
The B2 MuJoCo README instructs the user to install mujoco, enter the b2_description_mujoco directory and run 'simulate ./xml/scene.xml' to open the model.

The unitree_ros README says its ROS simulation packages load robots and joint controllers in Gazebo for low-level torque, position and angular-velocity control, and that the Gazebo simulation cannot do high-level walking.
The selected file is an MJCF scene named 'b2 scene' that includes b2.xml.
The scene adds a directional light and a plane floor geom named floor.
The included B2 model root is named b2 and its compiler element declares radian angles, meshdir ../meshes and autolimits true.
The B2 default class gives joints damping 1 and armature 0.1.
The base_link body starts at pos 0 0 0.8 and carries the free joint floating_base_joint.
The FL leg has a hip joint range -0.87 to 0.87 rad, a thigh joint range -0.94 to 4.69 rad and a calf joint range -2.82 to -0.43 rad; the FR, RL and RR legs declare the same ranges.
The actuator block declares twelve motor actuators: the hip and thigh motors have ctrlrange -200 to 200 and the calf motors have ctrlrange -300 to 300.
The model declares joint position and velocity sensors for the twelve leg joints plus body quaternion, gyro, accelerometer and frame-position sensors.
The keyframe named home sets a 19-value qpos with the base at 0 0 0.5 and the identity quaternion, and a 12-value ctrl.
unitree_guide's CMakeLists sets ROBOT_TYPE Go1 (Go1 and A1 supported), SIMULATION ON and REAL_ROBOT OFF.
With REAL_ROBOT on, unitree_guide defines COMPILE_WITH_REAL_ROBOT and, for A1, uses the unitree_legged_sdk_3.2 headers and libraries.
The vendored unitree_ros directory carries the BSD 3-Clause License of HangZhou YuShu Technology (Unitree Robotics).

determinism.notes: Event-driven placeholder integration with no contact, constraint or force solver; the same control input reproduces the same placeholder state hash, but this is a stand-in digest, not a MuJoCo trajectory or state-hash replay.

gaps: the fake is a package-local stand-in for the mujoco module: it parses the MJCF and its includes for model shape, actuator names and ctrlranges, but it loads no meshes, textures, inertias or contacts and runs no MuJoCo physics

each motor's control value accelerates its joint through a placeholder gain against a placeholder damping (a torque stand-in, not the model's inertia); the free base stays at qpos0, and gravity, contacts, friction, joint limits and sensor physics are not integrated
reset restores qpos0 parsed from the MJCF (base at 0 0 0.8, identity quaternion, hinges at 0), as mj_resetData does; the stand-in settles nothing by physics
the snapshot uses the bridge's basic profile (time, qpos, qvel, act and ctrl) because the stand-in exposes no full integration-state API; warm-start and derived quantities are not preserved
the upstream ROS 1 graph, Gazebo, unitree_guide, the controllers and the model's sensors are NOT COVERED
the published timestep_ms is the stand-in's placeholder step; the scene declares no option timestep, so this value is not a sourced model parameter and does not establish MuJoCo timing or determinism

measures.description: Declared native checkpoint. Integration profile restores the full native input vector; basic profile restores only advertised state plus actuator activation and exact native time. Neither profile certifies external callbacks, plugins, RNG or hardware fidelity.

safe_state.description: The simulation stops advancing: after an e-stop no cap.world.step.v1 or cap.world.reset.v1 call is accepted until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch, while the integration state stays readable.
